name: MA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district with a +15 partisan lean
Incumbent Stephen Lynch running with a large financial advantage
Republican opponent essentially unfunded, with negative cash on hand
Prediction markets price Lynch near 97% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Lynch: a +15 Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a fundraising gap of roughly $900,000 raised against a Republican challenger who is effectively broke. Markets price Lynch at about 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Lynch or an unexpectedly strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Boston's MA-08 is a heavily Democratic district, and veteran incumbent Stephen Lynch is seeking another term with the full advantages of incumbency. He has raised over $900,000 and holds more than $640,000 on hand, while Republican Robert Burke has raised almost nothing and reports negative cash on hand. A minor independent candidate is also on the ballot but lacks any visible campaign infrastructure.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money, both of which favor Lynch decisively. Prediction markets price his chances near 97%. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with the only real question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
